name: Receive a filled-in labsheet
description: read a labsheet back after the bench work and record what actually happened — the well each tube really went into, released holds for tubes nobody made, and a box brought into being if something landed in it. This is where the inventory learns anything true
phrases: update the inventory from a returned workbook

requires.note: prints by default; --write records and releases
resolves each slug's formula rather than trusting a cached value
the issue record this resolves against

returns: samples appended to the box's own file, holds released, and any proposed box created — or not, if nothing landed in it
notes: THE SHEET WINS. A hold says where the tube was expected; the returned sheet says where it went, and they disagree often — the student was at the freezer and we were not. The held well is let go either way. A tube nobody made records nothing, so an abandoned experiment leaves no trace. Rows are APPENDED, never re-serialized: a box's file carries comments and a column order somebody chose, and round-tripping it loses both.
